metadata.title: Alphabet Is In. Verizon Is Out.

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) rose 0.40% in premarket after S&P Global announced that the Google parent will replace Verizon (NYSE:VZ) in the Dow Jones Industrial Average ahead of Monday's open. Verizon fell 0.32% in premarket. S&P Global said Alphabet's inclusion would bolster the Dow's exposure to artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure, and advertising.
Alphabet joins Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) as the fifth mega-cap tech company in the 30-stock index. Verizon had represented just around half a percentage point of the Dow due to its low share price, a consequence of the index's price-weighted methodology. Honeywell International (NASDAQ:HON) will remain in the index under its new name, Honeywell Technologies, following the completion of its Honeywell Aerospace spinoff, though the spun-off entity will not be included.
Alphabet has raised $141 billion in debt and equity since October as part of its AI spending push. Despite closing its worst session in more than a year on Monday, Alphabet shares have more than doubled in the last year.
